title: Per-setup -2R daily stop that latches for the day (no re-arm when a later winner lifts realized R back above -2R), vs the live re-arming check
hypothesis: mcf/execution/risk.py blocks a setup only while its realized R(j) is <= -2R; the owner's rule reads 'a setup stops for the day at net -2R realized'. When a lot that was open at the trip closes in profit, realized R rises above -2R and the setup trades again. 10-20..10-22: 13 such re-arms, 55 entries after the first trip, -31.22R after costs (10-22: 10 re-arms, 42 entries, -28.71R). Largest: Graveyard RW2-exhaustion-noon-adv150-short-FD on 10-22 tripped at 10:15 (LEN, SYK stopped, -2.46R), CCL hit target at 10:28 (-1.84R), re-armed and opened 20 lots 10:40-11:01 (15 in the 11:00 poll), 18 stopped: -19.53R after the trip, day -21.38R (-$272). Replay on the live candidate set (ll1020 method, 9 sessions 10-12..10-22, Testing 1/2, GEN, Graveyard): latch2 +38.16R vs the live rule, 6 days better / 2 worse, day-clustered t 1.12 (bar 3.01); without 10-22 +7.54R.
notes: One configuration (latch2) on 9 live paper sessions; most of the gain is one setup-day (RW2-FD 10-22, +19.53R), so not evidence on its own. Owner decision LL-LATCH (inbox 2026-10-22) asks whether the live check should match the rule's wording; any change is a risk-code change after hours with tests + ledger. Related: LL-1.5 (-1.5R also avoided the RW2 re-arm because CCL's +0.65R left realized at -1.83R <= -1.5R). Educational only - not financial advice.
